title: create-local-table.sh reports any failure as 'Table already exists'
description: scripts/create-local-table.sh uses '2>/dev/null && ... || echo Table already exists', so a DynamoDB Local that is unreachable (e.g. Docker not running) is misreported as an existing table. Check specifically for ResourceInUseException and surface other errors. Also consider a Docker preflight check in the Makefile local-db target.

title: Add tooltip showing view count on daily chart
description: Add hover tooltips to the elm-charts line chart in Chart/Visits.elm so that hovering over a data point for a given day shows the date and view count. elm-charts 5.0.0 supports hover/tooltip features that are not currently used.
close_reason: Added hover tooltip using elm-charts built-in CE.onMouseMove/C.tooltip. Shows date and view count on hover.

title: Track visitor session duration and correlate with referrers
description:
Track how long each visitor stays on the site. This requires changes across the full stack:

**Tracker (tracker.js):** Capture session start time on page load, then send duration on page unload (e.g., via sendBeacon on visibilitychange/beforeunload). Could also track multi-page sessions.

**Backend (Haskell):** Add a new endpoint or extend /track to accept duration data. Update DynamoDB schema to store duration per visit.

**DynamoDB:** Store duration as an attribute on page view items. Consider how to aggregate duration by referrer efficiently.

**Dashboard (Elm):** Display average session duration alongside visit counts. Show duration breakdown by referrer so you can see if visits from a specific source tend to stay longer or shorter.

**Stats API:** Extend /stats response to include duration aggregations (average duration overall, average duration per referrer).

title: Enable GitHub Pages and cut the first Tallymark release
description:
After renaming the GitHub repo to `tallymark`:

- Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions (the `Website` workflow deploys `site/`).
- Push a `v0.1.0` tag to exercise `.github/workflows/release.yml` and confirm the bundle (`tallymark.tar.gz`, `function.zip`) attaches to the release.
- Check the site's `releases/latest/download/tallymark.tar.gz` link works.
- Prune build artifacts (backend/build, dashboard/build, elm-stuff) from git history before making the repo public.

title: Serve the dashboard over HTTPS via CloudFront
description: The dashboard is served from the S3 website endpoint over plain HTTP. Add an optional CloudFront distribution (with Origin Access Control, plus an optional custom domain and ACM cert parameter) to `infra/template.yaml`, and switch the bucket to private. Update the deploy guide's security notes.

title: Add a 'delete site data' control to the dashboard
description: `DELETE /sites?site=` exists and `Api.deleteSite` is defined in Elm but unused. Add a confirm-before-delete control in the dashboard (e.g. in the header next to the site picker).

title: Storage abstraction + HTTP server mode for the backend
description: Prerequisite for non-AWS deployments. Split the backend so the handlers depend on a small storage interface (writePageView, queryByDateRange, listSites, deleteSiteData) with DynamoDB as one implementation, and add a second entrypoint that serves the same routes over plain HTTP (e.g. warp) instead of the hal Lambda runtime.

title: Azure deployment (Functions custom handler + Table Storage)
description: Azure Functions supports custom handlers (any executable serving HTTP). Using the HTTP server mode, deploy the backend as a custom handler, implement a Table Storage or Cosmos DB storage backend, host the dashboard on Static Web Apps, and provide a Bicep template + deploy script. Depends on the storage abstraction issue.

title: Self-hosted server deployment (VPS / Ubicloud) with PostgreSQL or SQLite
description: Ubicloud has VMs, managed PostgreSQL and Kubernetes but no Lambda-style functions. Ship a long-running server build (HTTP server mode) with a PostgreSQL and/or SQLite storage backend, a Dockerfile/docker-compose, and docs for Ubicloud and any generic VPS. Depends on the storage abstraction issue.
